sentences.text: Bluejay maintains a time-stamped temperature history for each refrigerated medication compartment and raises an alarm when a configured limit is exceeded.
Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler applies approved upper and lower temperature limits to each monitored compartment.
Calibrated probes report readings at configured intervals, and the cooler records probe identity and calibration status with each reading.
Refrigerated stock is identified by medication, lot, and expiration date so that each unit remains traceable to its storage history.
When readings exceed a limit or a probe becomes unavailable, the affected stock is marked ineligible for routine dispensing.
The cooler preserves the affected stock in its current controlled environment while the condition is assessed.
Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler uses the handoff card to compare a transfer’s recorded custody time with its temperature history.
A Clinical Pharmacist reviews excursion details and determines whether affected stock may be released, quarantined, or discarded under pharmacy policy.
The cooler retains the disposition status against the affected lot and prevents stock marked ineligible from being selected for routine dispensing.
Authorized access to refrigerated compartments is recorded with the user identity, access time, and affected stock identifiers.
Door-open duration is monitored so that an access event that threatens temperature control can be distinguished from a brief inspection.
Temperature alarms remain active during loss of network connectivity, and local records are retained until communication is restored.
East Tube Dispatch Console maintains the approved route map and the current availability status of supported pneumatic segments.
East Tube Dispatch Console checks the selected route against the destination cabinet, current network availability, and approved routing configuration before releasing a capsule.
The console confirms that the destination is reachable and that the route does not include a segment reported unavailable.
Route selection uses the destination identifier and the latest approved configuration version rather than an operator-entered sequence of segments.
Before dispatch, the console checks for conflicting capsule movements and confirms that required interlocks are satisfied.
The Pneumatic Tube Network reports segment status, transfer progress, and delivery confirmation to the dispatch console.
If route status is stale or incomplete, the console holds the capsule and displays the condition for operator review.
A loss of communication with a route sensor prevents the console from treating the affected segment as available.
An interruption during transit is recorded with the capsule identifier, last confirmed location, and time of the interruption.
The console alerts a Pharmacy Technician when a transfer stops progressing or cannot be confirmed at its destination.
After recovery, the console requires refreshed segment status and an approved route decision before dispatch resumes.
Route and temperature records retain timestamps and equipment identifiers to support operational review and investigation.
